mainTopic: Sources for ידות and for נזירות taking effect on נזירות, and how בל יחל and בל תאחר apply to a נזיר.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier derivation. For the view that the Torah does not speak in everyday human language, the phrase 'נזיר להזיר' teaches that one נזירות can take effect on top of another. The גמרא then asks about the opposite view (דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם), which already uses 'נזיר להזיר' to teach ידות. The answer is that the unusual word 'להזיר', instead of the simpler 'ליזור', teaches both laws. The scholars of ארץ ישראל add that one תנא learns ידות from 'לנדר נדר' and another learns it from 'ככל היצא מפיו יעשה'. Next, the גמרא examines the ברייתא's claim that נזירות, like נדרים, carries בל יחל and בל תאחר. רבא explains that בל יחל adds a second prohibition when a נזיר eats or drinks. For בל תאחר, the case 'when I wish' is rejected. רבא then gives the case of 'I will not leave the world until I become a נזיר', which takes effect immediately, just like a גט given 'one hour before my death.'

steps.title: Finishing the earlier derivation: one נזירות can take effect on another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its previous point: for the view that every extra word in the Torah teaches something, the double phrase 'נזיר להזיר' teaches that נזירות takes effect on נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that a term of נזירות takes effect on a term of נזירות he already accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the tail end of a sentence that started before this section. It finishes the earlier teaching that the extra words 'נזיר להזיר' show that one נזירות can take effect on top of another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view holds that the Torah does not speak like ordinary people, so a doubled phrase must teach something new. Here the extra phrase is used to show that a second נזירות vow is valid even while the person is already a נזיר. The next step questions how the other view learns this.

keyTerms.meaning: The status of a נזיר, someone who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts, and contact with the dead
Takes effect on, lands on top of

phrases.english: that a term of naziriteship takes effect upon a term of naziriteship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the view that the Torah does not speak in human language, 'נזיר להזיר' teaches that נזירות takes effect on נזירות.

steps.title: How does the other view learn that one נזירות takes effect on another?
steps.stepSummary: For the view of דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם, which uses 'נזיר להזיר' for ידות, where is the source that נזירות takes effect on נזירות? This question only matters if that view agrees with the rule at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the Torah speaks in ordinary human language, and who uses 'נזיר להזיר' to teach that ידות of נזירות count as real נזירות, where does he learn that נזירות takes effect on נזירות? It is fine if he holds that it does NOT take effect. But if he holds that it does, where does he learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other view and asks for its source. That view has already 'used up' the phrase 'נזיר להזיר' to teach ידות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The view of דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם cannot learn from the doubled phrase 'לנדר נדר', so it learns ידות from 'נזיר להזיר'. That leaves no extra words to teach that נזירות takes effect on נזירות. The גמרא adds that this is only a problem if this view actually holds that rule. If it holds that a second נזירות does not take effect, no source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah speaks the way people normally speak, so doubled words don't always teach something extra

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. The one who says the Torah does NOT speak in human language learns ידות from 'לנדר נדר'. The one who says it DOES speak in human language must find ידות somewhere else, which is 'נזיר להזיר'.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source, for the view of דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם, that one נזירות takes effect on another.

steps.title: The unusual word 'להזיר' teaches two laws
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written the simpler word 'ליזור'. Choosing 'להזיר' shows it is teaching two things: ידות of נזירות, and נזירות taking effect on נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say 'ליזור'. Why does it say 'להזיר'? Learn two laws from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the specific form of the word 'להזיר' is unusual. That unusual form is enough to teach both laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the view of דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם agrees that a strange word choice can teach something. The simple form would be 'ליזור', so the longer 'להזיר' is a sign of an extra lesson. That lets this view learn both ידות and נזירות on top of נזירות from the same phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק say, meaning it could have said
The simpler form of 'to become a נזיר'
Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: Even someone who holds דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם will learn from an unusual word form. 'להזיר' instead of 'ליזור' teaches both ידות נזירות and נזירות חל על נזירות.

phrases.english: Let the verse say 'lizor',

phrases.english: Learn two things from it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The unusual form 'להזיר' (instead of 'ליזור') teaches both ידות נזירות and נזירות חל על נזירות.

steps.title: The scholars of ארץ ישראל: two sources for ידות
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they say one תנא learns ידות from 'לנדר נדר', and another learns it from 'ככל היצא מפיו יעשה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they say: there is a תנא who learns ידות from 'to vow a vow', and there is a תנא who learns it from 'he shall do according to all that comes out of his mouth'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a different tradition from ארץ ישראל about where the law of ידות comes from. It names two separate פסוקים, each used by a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first תנא holds the Torah does not speak in human language, so he learns ידות from the doubled 'לנדר נדר'. The second holds it does speak in human language, so he uses the broad word 'ככל' ('according to ALL') to include ידות. This gives a source for ידות of all vows, not only נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
A sage from the time of the משנה
Who derives it, who brings it out
He shall do according to all that comes out of his mouth

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows ידות can be learned for all נדרים, not only נזירות, even by those who hold דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One תנא learns ידות from 'לנדר נדר'; another learns it from 'ככל היצא מפיו יעשה'.

steps.title: Quoting the line from the ברייתא about vows and נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier ברייתא: just as נדרים carry בל יחל and בל תאחר, so does נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: Just as with vows a person transgresses 'he shall not profane' and 'you shall not delay', the same is true of נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא it brought earlier so it can examine it. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compared נזירות to נדרים: both carry בל יחל (breaking your word) and בל תאחר (being late to fulfill it). The גמרא will now check whether these two prohibitions can really happen with a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against breaking your word
The prohibition against delaying the fulfillment of a vow

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא the גמרא quoted earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: Just as with vows one transgresses
'he shall not profane' and 'you shall not delay'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the source of ידות back to another line of the earlier ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נזירות, like נדרים, carries בל יחל and בל תאחר.

steps.title: How can a נזיר ever break בל יחל?
steps.stepSummary: For a regular vow, בל יחל is easy to picture. A נזיר, though, seems to already be covered by בל יאכל and בל ישתה, so where does בל יחל come in?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, you can find בל יחל with vows: if someone says 'I will eat this loaf' and does not eat it, he breaks 'he shall not profane his word.' But how can you find בל יחל with נזירות? Once he says 'I am a נזיר' he is a נזיר. If he eats grapes, he breaks 'he shall not eat'. If he drinks wine, he breaks 'he shall not drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how בל יחל could ever apply to a נזיר, since he already has his own specific prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a regular vow, the only prohibition he breaks is בל יחל, so the case is clear. A נזיר becomes a נזיר the moment he speaks, and any breach is already covered by בל יאכל or בל ישתה. So the ברייתא's claim that נזירות carries בל יחל seems to have no case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted', meaning this part is fine; the problem comes next
'How can you find it?', asking for a real case
The נזיר's own prohibitions against eating grape products and drinking wine
'He stands in', meaning he is liable under that prohibition

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every breach by a נזיר is already covered by his own specific prohibitions, so no case is left for בל יחל.

steps.title: רבא: The נזיר breaks two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that בל יחל adds a second prohibition. A נזיר who eats or drinks breaks both his specific prohibition and בל יחל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes him transgress two prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that בל יחל does not need its own separate case. It is added on top of בל יאכל or בל ישתה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed בל יחל has to cover a case nothing else covers. רבא says it overlaps instead: one act of eating grapes or drinking wine breaks both the נזיר prohibition and בל יחל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To transgress it with two', meaning to be liable for two prohibitions for one act

phrases.english: רבא said:
To make him transgress two prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about בל יחל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the role of the prohibition: it adds to an existing one rather than needing its own case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בל יחל would need a case not already covered by בל יאכל or בל ישתה
steps.terutzMaskana: בל יחל adds a second prohibition to the same act

steps.title: How can a נזיר ever break בל תאחר?
steps.stepSummary: The same problem is raised for בל תאחר: a person becomes a נזיר the moment he speaks, so how can he ever be late?
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you find 'you shall not delay' with נזירות? Once he says 'I am a נזיר' he is a נזיר. If he eats, he breaks 'he shall not eat'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises the same kind of question about בל תאחר. If נזירות starts right away, there is no way to delay it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבא's answer does not help, because the problem is different. To delay a vow, there has to be a time gap before it takes effect. A plain 'I am a נזיר' takes effect at once, so there is no gap.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נזירות takes effect immediately, so there is no time left in which he could delay.

steps.title: First answer: he said 'when I wish'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a case where the נזירות does not start right away: he said 'I will be a נזיר when I wish.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he says, 'When I wish, I will be a נזיר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a case with a time gap: the person leaves the start of his נזירות open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he did not become a נזיר yet, there is room for delay, and the idea is that waiting too long would break בל תאחר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When I wish', leaving the start time up to himself

phrases.english: Where he says 'When I wish, I will be a נזיר.'

steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed only: a vow 'when I wish' would create a time gap. Step 10 rejects this, so it is not the final answer.

steps.title: 'When I wish' has no deadline
steps.stepSummary: The answer is rejected: if he said 'when I wish', he never has a deadline, so he can never be late.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said 'when I wish', there is no 'you shall not delay'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the last answer. A person who said 'when I wish' never misses a deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being late means missing a set time. 'When I wish' gives him the right to choose any time, so waiting is not a delay at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'There is not'

steps.title: רבא: 'I will not leave the world until I become a נזיר'
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new case: someone says he will not die before becoming a נזיר. He becomes a נזיר right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: For example, he said 'I will not leave the world until I become a נזיר.' From that moment he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new case for בל תאחר, and says this person is a נזיר from the moment he speaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His vow has a deadline: before he dies. Since he could die at any moment, his נזירות must start immediately, and putting it off risks missing the deadline.

steps.title: Proof from a גט given 'one hour before my death'
steps.stepSummary: רבא compares this to a man who gives his wife a גט to take effect one hour before his death. She may not eat תרומה right away, since he might die at any moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like one who says to his wife, 'Here is your גט, one hour before my death.' She is forbidden to eat תרומה immediately. We see that we say: at every moment, maybe he is about to die.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a case from גיטין to back up his claim that the נזירות starts right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גט case, the halacha treats every moment as possibly the hour before his death. So she is treated as possibly divorced already and cannot eat תרומה. The same reasoning will apply to the נזיר.

'We see from this', drawing a conclusion from a case

steps.title: So here too he is a נזיר at once
steps.stepSummary: Just like the גט, the person who vowed 'before I die' is a נזיר immediately, since he might die now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, he is a נזיר immediately, because we say: maybe he is about to die now.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the proof from the גט to the נזיר and closes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since every moment might be his last, his נזירות must start now. This gives a real case for בל תאחר: his vow has a deadline, his death, and he could fail to meet it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here too', applying the comparison
'Immediately'

steps.whatToRemember: בל יחל applies to a נזיר as a second prohibition on top of his own (רבא). בל תאחר applies in a case like 'I will not leave the world until I become a נזיר', which takes effect at once because he might die at any moment, just like a גט given 'one hour before my death.'

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A vow of נזירות with the deadline 'before I die' takes effect immediately, which gives a real case for בל תאחר.
